app-commands.description: Spec #3147 ST-1: the application command surface the built-in windows receive. build.rs registers an application manifest (tauri_build::AppManifest::commands), so from now on no command reaches a window unless a capability grants it. This capability grants the app-manifest default permission set (permissions/app/default.toml) to exactly the built-in window class, so the shipped applications keep every command they had before the gate was turned on. It matches NO installed-* label: since Spec #3146 the installed tier's isolation is cardinality plus exact set - exactly one capability (installed-app-commands.json) matches installed-* and it grants exactly allow-installed-app-invoke with no core:* permission, while every other capability, this one included, still matches no installed label.

default.description: Default capabilities for the Fredo desktop app

installed-app-commands.description: Spec #3146: the installed tier's ENTIRE authority surface. Exactly one command (`installed_app_invoke`), granted by exactly one permission (`allow-installed-app-invoke`), to exactly the installed window-label family (`installed-*`) — and no `core:*` permission, so an installed document cannot create a window, listen for events or drag. Every other capability still matches no installed label, so any other registered command stays ACL-refused to an installed window; the dispatcher then decides declared reach, consent and data ownership from the IPC webview's own window label. This file supersedes (does not delete) the #3147 invariant that zero capabilities reach `installed-*`: isolation is now cardinality plus exact-set. runtime::capability_guard pins all of it.

mcp-bridge-dev.description: DEV-ONLY debug bridge. The plugin is registered under #[cfg(debug_assertions)] in src/lib.rs, so this capability is inert in a release build (no bridge port, no commands). Do not add this file to an explicit app.security.capabilities list for release builds.
